THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 -4-  NC: 2023:KHC:20984  MFA No. 2643 of 2015  JUDGMENT

In this appeal, the petitioners have challenged the judgment dated 02.12.2013 passed in M.V.C.No.301/2013 on the file of the II Additional Senior Civil Judge and Additional M.A.C.T.-V,
Chitradurga ('the Tribunal' in short).
2. For the sake of convenience, parties shall be referred as per their status before the Trial Court.
Thippakka vs Mahadevappa on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119820961/
3

3. Briefly stated the facts are, on 28.11.2010 at about 8.30 p.m., one M.Thippeswamy, the deceased,
along with his wife Thippakka/petitioner No.1 and his son Lokesh/petitioner No.2 while travelling in a Tractor-Trailor bearing registration No.KA-17/TA-5746-5747 near Nayakanahatti met with head-on collision with another Tractor-Trailor bearing registration No.KA-16/TA-892-893 and sustained injuries.
The deceased was taken to Government Hospital, Nayakanahatty and then to District Hospital, Chitradurga for treatment, on 29.11.2010 at 4.50 p.m., he succumbed to death.
The petitioners being the wife and children, father and sister of the deceased approached the Tribunal under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.10,70,000/-.
Claim was opposed by the Insurance Companies of both the Tractors and the owner of the Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TA-892-893.

The Tribunal after taking the evidence recorded its finding that both the Tractors have equally contributed for the accident and assessed the compensation of Rs.5,33,000/- and directed the owners of both the Tractors to pay the compensation by dismissing the claim petition against the Insurance Companies.

Aggrieved by the same, the wife and children of the deceased have filed this appeal seeking for enhancement as well as questioning the liability fastened against the owners of the Tractors on various grounds.

5. Heard the arguments of Sri.H.Ashok Kumar, learned counsel for the petitioners,
Sri.D.Vijayakumar, learned counsel for respondent No.2/Insurance Company, NC:
2023:KHC:20984 Sri.Madhukar Nadig, learned counsel for respondent No.1/owner of the Tractor and Sri.H.S.Lingaraj, learned counsel for respondent No.4/Insurnace Company.
6.

It is the contention of the learned Counsel for the petitioners that for the accident of the year 2010, the Tribunal has taken the income at Rs.3,000/- and not considered the future prospects, so also the compensation under conventional heads and sought for enhancement.

It is further contended that the Tractors were covered with insurance and the insurer has to indemnify the insured and therefore, all the respondents have to pay the compensation.
7.

Per contra, learned counsel for respondent No.1/owner of the Tractor bearing No.KA-16/TA-892-893 contended that the Tribunal has taken the income of the deceased on the higher side, the compensation has been awarded under conventional heads disproportionately and sought for reduction of the compensation.
He contended that the insurance cover has taken to cover the risk of the NC: 2023:KHC:20984 passengers as well as the third party.
Hence, the liability of the first respondent has to be indemnified by the second respondent/insurer.
8. Learned counsel for the respondent No.2/insurer has contended that there is no valid insurance at the time of accident for the Tractor-Trailor in question.
The Tribunal has rightly recorded its finding and dismissed the claim and supported the impugned judgment.

9. Learned counsel for respondent No.4/insurer has argued in line with the respondent No.2 that there is no valid insurance for the passengers of Trailor and there is no question of indemnifying the owner.
The Tribunal has rightly dismissed the claim and the owner has to pay compensation.

Thippakka vs Mahadevappa on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119820961/
4 10.
I have given my anxious consideration to the arguments advanced on behalf of the parties and also perused the materials on record.

There is no dispute as to the accident, cause of accident, injuries sustained by the deceased and his death on account of accidental injuries, the petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are the wife and children of the deceased, petitioner No.5/father of the deceased is no more and petitioner No.6 is the married sister of the deceased and she cannot be treated as dependant of the deceased.
12. As pointed above, the accident was on 28.11.2010, the deceased was an agriculturist and for a person with no proof of income, notional income is assessed at Rs.5,500/-.

The principles laid down in National Insurance Co.Ltd. -vs- Pranay Sethi and Others1 and Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2, has to be followed regarding assessment of compensation so also multiplier.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

entities.text: Sarla Varma (Smt.) and Others -vs- Delhi Transport Corporation and Another2
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since one of the dependants is dead and 6th petitioner is not a dependant, there remains only wife and children of the deceased.
Therefore, the deduction (2017) 16 SCC 680 (2009) 6 SCC 121 NC: 2023:KHC:20984 towards personal expenses shall be 1/4th.
The deceased was aged 45 years and therefore, future prospects of a person with no proof of income shall be 25% of the income.

Then, the calculation of loss of dependency comes to Rs.5,500/- + Rs.1,375/-
(25% future prospects) = Rs.6,875/- minus Rs.1,718/- (1/4) = Rs.5,157/-x12x14 multiplier comes to Rs.8,66,376/-.
Towards conventional heads for four dependants, a sum of Rs.20,000/- each towards loss of love and affection and Rs.10,000/- each towards loss of estate and funeral expenses.

Then, the just compensation comes to Rs.9,66,376/- as against Rs.5,33,000/- assessed by the Tribunal, thereby the petitioners are entitled for enhancement of Rs.4,33,376/-.
13.

As regards liability is concerned, there is no dispute that the deceased and petitioner Nos.1 and 2 were travelling in the Trailor portion of the Tractor bearing No. No.KA-17/TA-5746 whereas, the Tractor-Trailor bearing registration No.KA-16/TA-892-893 was also involved in the accident, hence,
both have contributed equally.
There is - 10 - NC: 2023:KHC:20984 no insurance cover for the Trailor passenger and so also, the opposite Tractor has no insurance cover on the date of accident.
When there is no coverage of insurance, the Tribunal has rightly recorded its finding that respondent Nos.1 and 3 are liable to pay the compensation equally.
14. In view of the above, the claim of the petitioners for enhancement of compensation needs to be allowed in part and owners of both the Tractor and Trailors are held liable to pay the compensation.

In the result, the following:
ORDER (i) The appeal is allowed in part.

Thippakka vs Mahadevappa on 16 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/119820961/
5
(ii) The award passed by the Tribunal is hereby modified.
The petitioners would be entitled for enhanced compensation of Rs.4,33,376/- with interest @ 6% per annum from the date of petition till realization.

(iii) The respondent Nos.1 and 3/owners of both Tractors and Trailors are directed to pay the - 11 - NC: 2023:KHC:20984 compensation equally within a period of eight weeks from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
(iv) Rest of the order of the Tribunal is kept intact.
(v) The amount in deposit, if any, shall be transmitted to the Tribunal along with records forthwith.

Sd/-
